text: The engine computer detected combustion misfires on cylinder 1.
hint: Common causes: worn spark plug or failing ignition coil on that cylinder; swap the coil to another cylinder to see if the misfire follows it. Leaking injectors and intake-valve carbon are known N54 causes too.

text: The engine computer detected combustion misfires on cylinder 2.
hint: Common causes: worn spark plug or failing ignition coil on that cylinder; swap the coil to another cylinder to see if the misfire follows it. Leaking injectors and intake-valve carbon are known N54 causes too.

hint: Common causes: worn spark plug or failing ignition coil on that cylinder; swap the coil to another cylinder to see if the misfire follows it. Leaking injectors and intake-valve carbon are known N54 causes too.

text: The engine computer detected combustion misfires on cylinder 5.
hint: Common causes: worn spark plug or failing ignition coil on that cylinder; swap the coil to another cylinder to see if the misfire follows it. Leaking injectors and intake-valve carbon are known N54 causes too.

text: The engine computer detected combustion misfires on cylinder 6.
hint: Common causes: worn spark plug or failing ignition coil on that cylinder; swap the coil to another cylinder to see if the misfire follows it. Leaking injectors and intake-valve carbon are known N54 causes too.

text: The engine computer detected misfires on more than one cylinder.
hint: Check plugs and coils first; on N54 a cold-start misfire across one bank can point to leaking injectors (BMW SI B13 04 09) and general misfires to intake-valve carbon (SI B12 02 12). Read the per-cylinder codes stored alongside.

text: Misfires were detected while the fuel tank was nearly empty.
hint: Refuel and clear the code before chasing ignition or injector faults.

text: Fuel injection on one or more cylinders was cut because high-pressure fuel rail pressure was too low.
hint: Classic N54 high-pressure fuel pump (HPFP) code, but a weak in-tank low-pressure pump or clogged filter can cause it too; check low-side pressure before buying an HPFP. BMW extended HPFP coverage on many N54 cars (SI B12 55 06).

text: High-pressure fuel rail pressure dropped below the target the engine computer asked for.
hint: Common cause: failing HPFP; also check the low-pressure supply (in-tank pump, filter) since either side can trigger it.

text: Measured high-pressure fuel rail pressure does not make sense compared with what the pump control expects.
hint: Often stored together with 29F2 or 29DC; diagnose the fuel supply (HPFP, low-pressure pump, rail pressure sensor) as a whole.

text: Fuel rail pressure was too low at the moment injection was enabled during start-up.
hint: Usually shows as long cranking. BMW's first fix was a DME software update; persistent cases point to the HPFP or low-pressure supply.

text: Fuel rail pressure fell away abnormally after the engine was switched off.
hint: A single occurrence is often harmless and can be cleared; if it returns with long cranks, suspect the HPFP or a leaking injector.

text: The fuel rail pressure sensor signal is faulty or implausible.
hint: Can be the rail pressure sensor or wiring, but often logged alongside 29DC when rail pressure genuinely collapses from a failing pump.

text: Problem with the signal to the volume control valve on the high-pressure fuel pump.
hint: Not a pressure code itself; check the valve's connector and wiring on the HPFP before replacing parts.
notes: Owner threads also show 2FBC stored with HPFP failures (e.g. https://www.e90post.com/forums/showthread.php?t=640139), but only one source states the meaning.

text: The low-pressure (in-tank) fuel supply did not reach the pressure the engine computer requested.
hint: Common on tuned cars. If it appears with other fuel codes, check the in-tank fuel pump, fuel filter and the fuel pump control module (EKPS).

text: Electrical fault in the low-pressure fuel sensor circuit.
hint: This is a wiring/sensor fault, not a pressure problem: check the low-pressure sensor and its plug first.

text: Fuel mixture control on bank 1 (cylinders 1-3) is outside its limits.
hint: Common causes: air leaks, oxygen sensor faults, injectors or tuning. If 29E1 is also stored, suspect a cause affecting both banks.

text: Fuel mixture control on bank 2 (cylinders 4-6) is outside its limits.
hint: Common causes: air leaks, oxygen sensor faults, injectors or tuning. If 29E0 is also stored, suspect a cause affecting both banks.

text: Injector calibration values stored in the engine computer are implausible.
hint: Typical after injector replacement: the new injectors' calibration (IMA) codes must be entered into the DME.

text: Boost (charge-air) pressure is lower than the engine computer expects (underboost).
hint: Common causes: boost leaks in charge pipe/intercooler/diverter valves, cracked wastegate vacuum lines, faulty boost solenoids, worn or rattling wastegates, or a failing turbo.

text: Boost (charge-air) pressure is higher than the engine computer expects (overboost).
hint: Common causes: tuning, or boost solenoids/vacuum control letting the wastegates close too much.

text: Boost pressure control has been switched off, so the engine runs without boost.
hint: Usually a follow-on fault: read the other stored codes (VANOS, overheating, boost faults) and fix those first; alone it may just need clearing.

text: Problem with the wastegate control input signal.
hint: Most often an unplugged wastegate/boost solenoid connector or loose wiring, sometimes caused by a piggyback tuning module.
notes: Owner threads show 30CF with 3100 after tuner installs (e.g. https://www.e90post.com/forums/showthread.php?t=1168149) but do not state the meaning.

text: Intake camshaft VANOS is sluggish or stuck and does not reach its target position.
hint: BMW bulletins point to low oil pressure at the VANOS, clogged or failed VANOS solenoids, or a missing oil filter cap insert; often fixed by replacing both solenoids and changing the oil.
notes: Same code and meaning also used on N51/N52 MSV DMEs per the bulletins. N55 (MEVD17.2) reports VANOS faults under different codes (2D5A etc.).

text: Exhaust camshaft VANOS is sluggish or stuck and does not reach its target position.
hint: BMW bulletins point to low oil pressure at the VANOS, clogged or failed VANOS solenoids, or a missing oil filter cap insert; often fixed by replacing both solenoids and changing the oil.
notes: Same code and meaning also used on N51/N52 MSV DMEs per the bulletins. N55 (MEVD17.2) reports VANOS faults under different codes (2D60 etc.).

text: Crankshaft and intake camshaft positions are not synchronised as expected.
hint: Common causes: intake VANOS solenoid or oil supply problems, camshaft or crank sensor signal faults, or timing problems; can cause crank-no-start.

text: Crankshaft and exhaust camshaft positions do not correlate as expected.
hint: Check exhaust VANOS solenoid, VANOS unit and its bolts, and the exhaust cam sensor before suspecting timing.
notes: Meaning agrees across sources for E9x, but N54-specific attribution rests on a single 335i Q&A thread.

text: The electric coolant pump is not running at the speed the engine computer asked for.
hint: Common cause on N54/N55: the electric water pump is failing (typical at 60k-100k miles); check its connector and wiring first.

text: The electric coolant pump has shut itself off.
hint: Treat as urgent: stop driving if the temperature warning comes on. Common cause on N54/N55: the electric water pump is failing (typical at 60k-100k miles); check its connector and wiring first.

text: The electric coolant pump is running in a reduced-power mode.
hint: Early warning of pump trouble; also check coolant level and bleed air from the system.

text: The engine computer cannot communicate with the electric coolant pump over its data line (BSD).
hint: Check the pump connector, wiring and fuse for corrosion or damage before replacing the pump.

text: Intake VANOS control fault: the intake camshaft is sticking.
hint: BMW bulletin cause on early N55 (2010 build): failed VANOS adjuster units or loose/broken adjuster bolts; also check oil level and the VANOS solenoids.
notes: E9x N55 (MEVD17.2) code per BMW SI B12 14 12, which also covers E82/E88 135i and E70/E71; F-series N55 uses 6-digit codes instead.

text: Intake VANOS control fault: the intake camshaft does not reach its target position.
hint: BMW bulletin cause on early N55 (2010 build): failed VANOS adjuster units or loose/broken adjuster bolts; also check oil level and the VANOS solenoids.
